requirements.requirement: Initialize and update Key and V with the prescribed 0x00 and optional 0x01 rounds.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Key begins as all zeroes, V as all ones, and Update performs both prescribed HMAC rounds when provided_data is nonempty.
requirements.securityImpact: The core state transition is structurally equivalent to the standard.

requirements.requirement: Seed material is entropy_input || nonce || personalization_string and reseed_counter is set to 1.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Instantiate concatenates those inputs in order, updates the initial state, and the session constructor sets reseed_counter to 1.
requirements.securityImpact: Production input ordering and state initialization are correct.

requirements.requirement: Security strength must be one of the permitted values and no greater than the hash mechanism maximum.
requirements.moseraImplementation: The runtime accepts every integer at least 128 and does not reject SHA-256 requests above 256 bits or non-table values.
requirements.securityImpact: The reusable production runtime can accept an unsupported security-strength claim, although the canonical caller passes 256 for SHA-256.
requirements.remediation: In a new qualified baseline, enforce the permitted security strengths and each hash function's maximum strength before instantiation.

requirements.requirement: Instantiation obtains entropy meeting the requested strength and a nonce satisfying the applicable entropy or uniqueness requirement.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Production requests 48 bytes of OS entropy and a separate 32-byte OS nonce, but the low-level runtime checks only entropy byte length and accepts an empty nonce.
requirements.securityImpact: Canonical production parameters are defensible assuming the OS source, but the runtime API does not enforce the nonce contract.
requirements.remediation: Enforce the nonce requirement at the runtime boundary or make production-safe construction the only callable instantiation path.

requirements.requirement: Reseed uses entropy_input || additional_input, updates state, and resets reseed_counter to 1.
requirements.moseraImplementation: The state transition and counter reset match the pseudocode.
requirements.securityImpact: The reseed transition itself is correct.

requirements.requirement: Reseed entropy input provides at least the instantiated security strength.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Production obtains 48 fresh OS bytes, but Reseed accepts empty or undersized entropy without validation.
requirements.securityImpact: Future callers can perform a nominal reseed without the required entropy while the runtime reports success.
requirements.remediation: Enforce reseed entropy length/assurance against session.SecurityStrengthBits in a new qualified source version.

requirements.requirement: Generate updates with additional input before output, emits leftmost bits from repeated HMAC(K,V), updates again after output, and increments reseed_counter.
requirements.moseraImplementation: All prescribed state transitions are present; the same additional input is used for both updates.
requirements.securityImpact: The core generation transition is structurally correct.

requirements.requirement: A Generate request must not exceed 2^19 bits (65,536 bytes).
requirements.moseraImplementation: Generate checks only that byteCount is positive. The qualification generator requests 1,048,576 bytes in one call; the canonical outcome sampler requests 8 bytes per call.
requirements.securityImpact: The implementation and CSPRNG-1.2 sample-generation invocation exceed a normative per-request limit; statistical results remain empirical evidence but are not conforming Generate invocations.
requirements.remediation: Enforce 65,536 bytes per Generate call, lower qualification chunks to the limit, establish a new source hash, and determine the required statistical requalification scope.

requirements.requirement: Generate must require reseed when reseed_counter exceeds 2^48.
requirements.moseraImplementation: ReseedCounter is incremented but never checked before generation and has no standards-specific overflow guard.
requirements.securityImpact: Canonical short-lived sessions will not practically reach the limit, but the reusable runtime does not enforce the normative state-machine boundary.
requirements.remediation: Reject Generate when the session exceeds the 2^48 request interval and require reseed.

requirements.requirement: HMAC_DRBG uses an approved hash and output length appropriate to that hash.
requirements.moseraImplementation: The runtime delegates to .NET HMACSHA256, HMACSHA384, and HMACSHA512 and uses 32, 48, and 64-byte state values.
requirements.securityImpact: Correctness depends on the .NET and platform cryptographic implementations.
requirements.remediation: External validation must accept or validate the deployed .NET/platform cryptographic boundary.

requirements.requirement: DRBG state is protected and uninstantiation makes state unavailable.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Per-session Key, V, previous block, and output-hash state are explicitly zeroed on Destroy/Dispose; production always destroys in finally.
requirements.securityImpact: Logical state destruction is implemented; managed runtime copies and process dumps remain outside strict zeroization guarantees.
requirements.remediation: Document managed-memory limits and tighten exceptional temporary-buffer cleanup.

requirements.requirement: Prediction resistance is claimed only when fresh entropy is obtained for each request under the defined semantics.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Mosera performs fresh per-draw instantiate and immediate reseed but exposes no prediction-resistance request flag and does not reseed before every bounded sample.
requirements.securityImpact: The operational design is conservative but must not be described as SP 800-90A prediction resistance.
requirements.remediation: Keep the claim explicitly prohibited unless a separate design implements and validates prediction-resistance semantics.

requirements.requirement: Known-answer and health tests detect implementation or catastrophic failures according to the applicable validation boundary.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Startup readiness executes three deterministic fixtures and output blocks undergo a repetition test.
requirements.securityImpact: The fixtures exercise transitions but are not traceably identified CAVP vectors, and the continuous test is an internal defense rather than entropy-source validation.
requirements.remediation: Import authoritative NIST/CAVP vector material with source identifiers and expected values generated outside Mosera.

requirements.requirement: Entropy claims require characterization, health testing, and validation of the entropy source within its defined boundary.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Mosera requests bytes from getrandom, BCryptGenRandom, or SecRandomCopyBytes and verifies success, but does not characterize or validate those OS entropy sources.
requirements.securityImpact: Mosera may claim use of OS cryptographic entropy APIs, not SP 800-90B validation or 256 bits of validated entropy assurance.
requirements.remediation: Obtain platform/module evidence or use an accepted validated entropy boundary for formal certification.

requirements.requirement: An entropy acquisition failure must not silently produce deterministic fallback input.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Each supported OS API throws on failure; unsupported platforms throw; Linux loops over partial reads; no fallback or cache exists.
requirements.securityImpact: Application behavior is fail-closed; entropy quality remains an OS/platform assumption.

requirements.requirement: An RBG2 construction combines a DRBG with a validated entropy source inside the defined RBG security boundary/module.
requirements.moseraImplementation: The architecture resembles RBG2 because it instantiates/reseeds HMAC_DRBG from an OS source, but no evidence places a validated 90B entropy source in the same validated RBG boundary.
requirements.securityImpact: No defensible formal SP 800-90C conformity claim is currently available.
requirements.remediation: Resolve the validated entropy/module boundary and the SP 800-90A findings before selecting a formal 90C construction claim.

requirements.requirement: Each authoritative draw uses isolated mutable DRBG state.
requirements.moseraImplementation: The registered HmacDrbgRuntime is stateless; Instantiate creates a new local session and production destroys it in finally.
requirements.securityImpact: Concurrent draws do not share DRBG Key/V state.

requirements.requirement: Concurrent execution cannot accept two outcomes for one immutable execution manifest.
requirements.moseraImplementation: A manifest-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock wraps provider resolution, claim, generation, and completion; duplicate requests restore persisted evidence.
requirements.securityImpact: Database idempotency and cryptographic state isolation reinforce one authoritative result.

requirements.requirement: The manifest-bound provider is exact and there is no silent fallback across provider categories.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Resolution binds exact provider/configuration versions; the canonical orchestrator invokes only the selected category and rejects missing ingestion evidence.
requirements.securityImpact: A caller cannot substitute CSPRNG for official/manual evidence or vice versa.

requirements.requirement: Generated values are hash-bound to the draw, manifest, provider evidence, certificate, and canonical published outcome.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Canonical result bytes include draw/manifest/definition/evaluator/numbers/source hash; binding verifies the generated result hash and exact certificate/signing configuration before append-only publication.
requirements.securityImpact: Replacement, cross-draw substitution, and payload mutation are detected or rejected in the canonical production path.

requirements.requirement: Mapping random words to a bounded range introduces no modulo bias.
requirements.moseraImplementation: A 64-bit rejection threshold discards the incomplete residue before modulo reduction.
requirements.securityImpact: Every accepted 64-bit value maps uniformly to the target range.
requirements.remediation: Optionally define byte order explicitly for cross-architecture deterministic test portability.

requirements.requirement: Every ordered sample and therefore every unordered combination has the intended probability.
requirements.moseraImplementation: For position i, the sampler selects uniformly from i through n-1 and swaps; optional ascending sort occurs only after selection.
requirements.securityImpact: Keno/Matrix combinations are uniform under uniform bounded draws; sorting changes presentation, not selection probability.

requirements.requirement: Raw entropy, nonce, reseed material, and DRBG state are not persisted or logged.
requirements.moseraImplementation: The production provider persists generated numbers, hashes, health data, and identifiers only; SQL rejects fields named as raw secret material.
requirements.securityImpact: No raw RNG secret was found in production persistence or logging.

requirements.requirement: Hashes of secret initialization material exist only when necessary and justified.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Production SeedIdentifier is SHA-256(entropy || nonce || personalization) and is persisted; the older DRBG evidence contract also requires nonce and seed commitment hashes, though no production writer uses that table.
requirements.securityImpact: High-entropy preimage resistance prevents practical recovery, but the persisted verifier is unnecessary and expands evidence exposure without proving entropy quality.
requirements.remediation: Remove secret-derived identifiers in a versioned evidence contract and retain non-secret execution IDs, source identity, timestamps, output/result hashes, and configuration provenance.

requirements.requirement: A claim of official vectors is traceable to authoritative vector material and configuration identifiers.
requirements.moseraImplementation: Expected values are hardcoded for Mosera-defined sequential inputs and a source label mentions NIST, but no CAVP vector set/COUNT identifiers or external source artifact are recorded.
requirements.securityImpact: The tests are valuable regression fixtures but do not establish CAVP validation or independently sourced expected outputs.
requirements.remediation: Add traceable authoritative CAVP vectors as qualification-only evidence without replacing preserved regression fixtures.
